topic: Lower GI bleeding risk stratification (Oakland score)

audits.title: 81 Audit of Use of Oakland Score on Patients Presenting with PR Bleeding and Effect on Admissions with Retrospective Application
audits.standard: Validated Oakland Score for safe discharge of patients presenting with PR bleeding (discharge thresholds of 8 and 10 tested)

cycle1.result: 0/72 patients had an Oakland Score on initial clerking. On retrospective application, 41/75 (55%) (threshold 8) and 42/75 (56%) (threshold 10) were admitted or discharged correctly.

audits.other_findings: A threshold of 8 would have increased admissions by 20/37 (54%) and a threshold of 10 by 3/37 (8.1%); 88 notes were reviewed and 75 included.
audits.citation: Todd J, Wilkin R. 81 Audit of Use of Oakland Score on Patients Presenting with PR Bleeding and Effect on Admissions with Retrospective Application. British Journal of Surgery. 2023;110(Supplement_7). doi:10.1093/bjs/znad258.080.

audits.title: 946 A Complete Cycle Audit of the Appropriate Management of Stable Patients Presenting Acutely with a Lower GI Bleed Using the Oakland Score Risk Stratification Tool in Order to Avoid Unnecessary Admissions
audits.standard: British Society of Gastroenterology guidance on Oakland score risk stratification (safe discharge threshold ≤8)
audits.setting: University Hospital Lewisham, district general hospital

cycle1.result: 6/63 (10%) had a documented Oakland score; three patients with OS <8 were inappropriately admitted.

audits.intervention: Tailored teaching with a summary sheet and link to an e-calculator, after a departmental survey.

cycle2.result: 16/38 (42%) had a documented Oakland score; all 8/8 with OS ≤8 appropriately discharged.

audits.other_findings: Survey of 11 surgical team members: 27% (3/11) aware of the Oakland score and 9% (1/11) used it.
audits.citation: Sharma V, Smith E, Satar I, Birch D. 946 A Complete Cycle Audit of the Appropriate Management of Stable Patients Presenting Acutely with a Lower GI Bleed Using the Oakland Score Risk Stratification Tool in Order to Avoid Unnecessary Admissions. British Journal of Surgery. 2023;110(Supplement_7). doi:10.1093/bjs/znad258.160.

audits.title: Lower GI bleed audit
audits.standard: BSG guidelines on risk stratification with Shock Index and Oakland score
audits.setting: A&E and emergency general surgery, Salford Royal NHS Trust

cycle1.result: 1 patient (3%) had shock index documented; Oakland score rarely used.

audits.other_findings: 16 (44%) admitted under EGS, of whom 7 (44%) needed inpatient endoscopy and 3 (19%) transfusion; 2 (6%) needed CT angiogram.
audits.citation: Dasa M, Peters P, Bose S, Adeboye O. Lower GI bleed audit. British Journal of Surgery. 2023;110(Supplement_10). doi:10.1093/bjs/znad388.011.

audits.title: EP127 - Audit on Acute PR Bleed Admissions to the Surgical Assessment Unit and the Use of the Shock Index and Oakland Score
audits.standard: British Society of Gastroenterology: Shock Index (≤1) and Oakland Score (≤8) for safe discharge in acute PR bleeding
audits.setting: Surgical assessment unit, Bradford Royal Infirmary (large teaching hospital)

cycle1.result: SI documented in 0/37 and OS calculated in 1/37 at clerking; 12/34 (35%) managed appropriately; by OS, 20/34 (58.9%) incorrectly discharged.

audits.other_findings: Two patients had an unnecessary CTA.
audits.citation: Arshad S, Lockwood S. EP127 - Audit on Acute PR Bleed Admissions to the Surgical Assessment Unit and the Use of the Shock Index and Oakland Score. British Journal of Surgery. 2024;111(Supplement_8). doi:10.1093/bjs/znae197.445.

audits.title: TPW 4.11 Audit of Knowledge and Utilization of Oakland Scores for Lower GI Bleeds in Ulster Hospital Dundonald (UHD)
audits.standard: British Society of Gastroenterology 2019 guidelines: Oakland score to risk-stratify lower GI bleeding
audits.setting: Emergency Department referrals to surgery, Ulster Hospital Dundonald
audits.intervention: Posters in ED and seminar rooms and a departmental teaching session.
audits.other_findings: 61.8% of 34 surveyed clinicians were unaware of the Oakland score at baseline.

audits.title: TPTh 2.14 Enhancing Guideline Adherence in Lower Gastrointestinal Bleeding Through Structured Risk Stratification: A Two-Cycle Audit
audits.standard: BSG risk stratification guidance for lower gastrointestinal bleeding (Shock Index and Oakland score)
audits.setting: Acute tertiary hospital, Sir Salimullah Medical College and Hospital

cycle1.result: Shock Index calculated in 27% (18/66), Oakland score in 36% (24/66); admission rate 53% (35/66); 44% (15/35) of admitted patients had Oakland scores consistent with safe discharge.

cycle2.result: Shock Index 82% (47/57), Oakland score 79% (45/57); admission rate 38% (22/57); 18% (4/22) of admitted patients had Oakland scores consistent with safe discharge.

audits.other_findings: Reduced avoidable admissions with reported cost savings.
audits.citation: Sikder D, Saha G, Dey D. TPTh 2.14 Enhancing Guideline Adherence in Lower Gastrointestinal Bleeding Through Structured Risk Stratification: A Two-Cycle Audit. British Journal of Surgery. 2026;113(Supplement_8). doi:10.1093/bjs/znag087.439.
